questions.question: An application on an EC2 instance needs to read objects from S3. What is the recommended way to grant access?
options: Store an IAM user's access keys on the instance
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
Put the instance in an IAM group
questions.explanation: An EC2 instance role lets the service act on your behalf without stored keys; stored or root credentials are insecure, and groups contain users only.

questions.question: A security team must list every IAM user and whether each has MFA and active access keys. Which tool should they use?
questions.explanation: The Credentials Report is account-level and lists all users' credential status; Access Advisor is per user, the password policy sets rules, and CLI profiles are local configuration.

questions.question: An administrator wants to remove permissions a developer has but never uses. Which tool shows the evidence?
questions.explanation: Access Advisor shows granted services and when they were last accessed, guiding policy tightening; the Credentials Report covers credential status, not service usage.

questions.question: Two contractors share one IAM user to save time. Which best practice does this violate?
options: One physical user = one AWS user
Use access keys for the CLI
questions.explanation: Each person needs their own user for accountability; the other practices are unrelated to sharing a user identity.

questions.question: A Lambda function must write to a DynamoDB table. How should it receive permissions?
options: An IAM user with access keys in environment variables
questions.explanation: Lambda function roles let the service act on your behalf; embedded user keys and root are insecure, and functions cannot join IAM groups.

questions.question: Which pairing of tool and scope is correct?
questions.explanation: The Credentials Report is account level and Access Advisor is user level; IAM is global so Region level is wrong.

questions.question: Which is an IAM best practice from the course?
options: Assign permissions directly to every user
Use the root account for daily tasks
Assign users to groups and permissions to groups
Share access keys within a team
questions.explanation: Group-based permissions are a listed best practice; direct per-user permissions, daily root use and shared keys contradict it.
